change.title: pr-40940-flat
change.description: Fix concurrent group access to prevent NullPointerException
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null for a missing group, which breaks the GroupModel contract
findings.body:
The NPE is replaced by `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount()`. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount is documented as "Never returns null" (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/GroupModel.java:296). The PR body does not mention this change of contract.

What a caller sees: RealmCacheSession.getGroupById returns a cached adapter without checking the database when the entry is cached and not invalidated (model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/RealmCacheSession.java:964-985). For a group whose row is already gone, the group is still listed, and populateSubGroupCount stores null (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:90). The admin UI tests the count with `!== 0` (js/apps/admin-ui/src/components/group/GroupPickerDialog.tsx:324), so null is not read as zero.

Before, the request failed with an NPE. Now it succeeds silently with a removed group still listed and no count. Either the null is accepted and GroupModel's contract is updated, or the stale entry is dropped or the group omitted. That choice belongs to the author.

findings.title: The same concurrent NPE remains in the sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body:
The title says the PR prevents NullPointerException under concurrent group access. The same unguarded pattern remains in this file: `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` at lines 256, 262 and 268 has no null check. This path is reached from services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:180 (`group.getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1)`). If the group row was removed while its cached adapter is still served, that call throws the same NPE the PR fixes for getSubGroupsCount.

The guard for these methods needs a decision on what to return (for example an empty stream), so the author should either apply it here or state that these are out of scope.

findings.title: Reader thread is never stopped on failure and is not joined before the assertion
findings.body:
Two problems in the new test:

1. `deletedAll.set(true)` (line 155) runs only if every `remove()` in lines 152-154 succeeds. If one throws, the test fails but the reader thread (lines 139-149), created with the default non-daemon status, loops forever and keeps sending admin requests. That can hang the JVM or leave load on the shared test server.
2. The thread is not joined, so the assertion at line 157 can run while the reader is still inside a request. An exception raised by that last request is then missed.

Fix: put the delete loop and the flag in try/finally, join the reader thread, and only then assert on `caughtExceptions`.

findings.title: Does this test fail on the pre-fix code?
findings.body: The reader only checks that no exception escapes the listing call. The NPE needs a cached group whose database row is already removed, which means the window between the delete and the cache invalidation. Nothing in the test forces that window, so the test may pass on the code before the GroupAdapter change. I did not run it (the review is read-only). Did you confirm that it fails without the fix? If the timing is too narrow, a deterministic setup would be better.

findings.title: Test name and variable name do not describe the regression
findings.body: `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` says nothing about concurrent reads during deletes, and it has no reference to the bug (the PR body does not name an issue). The variable `groupUuuids` (lines 121, 129, 152) has a typo. A name such as `listGroupsWhileDeletingConcurrently` and a short comment linking the NPE would make the intent clear.

findings.title: Unrelated dead-code removal in a concurrency fix
findings.body: The private method `groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement` was removed. It had no callers in this file, and the diff does not touch any caller, so the removal is safe. It is unrelated to the NPE fix, though. Consider moving it to its own change or mentioning it in the PR body.

findings.title: Parent lookup can return null here; does the hierarchy path still throw on concurrent removal?
findings.body: Line 47 takes `parentModel` from `session.groups().getGroupById(...)` without a null check. Lines 51 and 56-57 then pass it to `canView` and `toRepresentation`. If the parent row is gone and not cached, the cache returns null (RealmCacheSession.java:973), and this path would throw the NPE the PR is meant to remove. The dereference inside `ModelToRepresentation` is not confirmed here, so this is a question about the author's intent, not a verified defect. Does the concurrency fix need to cover this path too?

contracts.action: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() on a cached group, reached from the group list (populateSubGroupCount) and group-by-id responses
contracts.equivalent_path: model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/GroupAdapter.java:190 (JPA count query); sibling lookup pattern in GroupAdapter.java:254-257 (modelSupplier.get())
contracts.before_after: Before: getGroupModel() performed a fresh database lookup and then called .getSubGroupsCount() unguarded, so a missing row threw an NPE. After: the lookup goes through the memoized modelSupplier, a null model returns null, and a non-null model returns its count. LazyModel memoizes only non-null values (LazyModel.java:15-20), so a null result is looked up again on the next call.
contracts.visible_effect: For a group whose row is gone while the cache still serves it, the response has a null subGroupCount instead of an error (GroupUtils.java:89-92). The admin UI tests subGroupCount with !== 0 (GroupPickerDialog.tsx:324).
contracts.failure_mode: Silent null count for a group that no longer exists in the database. This breaks the documented non-null contract at GroupModel.java:296, and the removed group is still listed because the cache is served without a database check (RealmCacheSession.java:964-985).

contracts.action: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, first, max), reached from the subgroup listing endpoint; unchanged by this PR
contracts.before_after: Unchanged: modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. The new null guard in getSubGroupsCount is not applied here.
contracts.visible_effect: If the parent group's row was removed while its cached adapter is still served, the request throws an NullPointerException from the resource method.
contracts.failure_mode: NullPointerException on a concurrently removed parent group. This is the same failure the PR claims to fix, left in place in the same class.
contracts.open_question: Confirm that the group in GroupResource comes from the cache-backed getGroupById, so that a stale adapter can reach line 180. The exception mapping for an NPE on this path was not read.

summary: Four files reviewed. The CachedGroup @Override is correct (InRealm declares getRealm), and the GroupUtils removal is safe because the method was private and unreferenced. The GroupAdapter change stops the NPE in getSubGroupsCount, but it returns null, which breaks the documented "never null" contract (GroupModel.java:296), and it silently lists a removed group with no count. The same NPE remains in the sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads, reached from GroupResource.java:180. The new test has a fix-level robustness problem: the reader thread is not stopped in a finally and not joined before the assertion, so a failing delete leaves it spinning and the last exception can be missed. Whether the test reproduces the race at all is unconfirmed, since I did not run it. I did not build or run anything; all claims come from reading the code.
